孤.meaning: In a pumpkin patch, one <part>melon</part> grows all by itself, with no vine-mates and no family. A <part>child</part> spots it, draws it a smile and wheels it home in a wagon to sit by the fire. Every lonely <kanji>orphan</kanji> deserves a home.
孤.on: Her pet <sound>ko</sound>ala hugs the melon all night so it never feels alone.

殿.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> and her little brother build a snowman <part>together</part>, give him a <part>flag</part> for a walking stick and argue all afternoon about his name. They run out of paint after the first two letters and a dot, so that's all his hat says: <kanji>Mr.</kanji>
殿.on: Their dad, a <sound>den</sound>tist, gives the snowman a full set of pebble teeth.
殿.kun: The snowman gets a <sound>to</sound>p hat, <sound>no</sound>t a cap, to go with his new name.

雲.meaning: A girl's <part>kite</part> climbs so high it tangles in something fluffy and grey and drags it home like a balloon. She ties it to her bedpost, where it drips <part>rain</part> on her goldfish all night. Her new pet is a <kanji>cloud</kanji>.
雲.on: She feeds it rainwater from a sp<sound>oon</sound> every morning.
雲.kun: Her mum, the <sound>coo</sound>k, follows it round the house with a <sound>mo</sound>p.

屯.meaning: A drill sergeant draws a <part>slash</part> in the mud and orders the troops to sleep behind it, then finds a <part>sprout</part> poking up in the middle of the camp. He waters it every dawn, salutes it, and gives it its own bunk in the <kanji>barracks</kanji>.
屯.on: In the mess hall, he serves its water with a giant pair of <sound>ton</sound>gs.
屯.kun: On Fridays the troops eat a <sound>ta</sound>co, ride a <sound>moo</sound>se and launch a toy <sound>ro</sound>cket.

純.meaning: At a market, a seller swears his silk is real. To prove it, he ties a single <part>thread</part> from a <part>hitching post</part> to a bull and lets it pull. The bull strains, the post creaks, the thread holds. The crowd buys every roll: it's <kanji>genuine</kanji>.
純.on: The bull gets a whole <sound>jun</sound>iper bush to munch as thanks.

遇.meaning: A <part>gumball machine</part> tips over at the top of a <part>ramp</part>, and every gumball rolls down, red, blue, green, clacking into one friendly heap at the bottom. Strangers kneel to pick them up and end up chatting. What a way to <kanji>meet</kanji>.
遇.on: Two of them get stuck together in a blob of <sound>goo</sound> and refuse to let go.
遇.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, it's you!' says one stranger to another, waving a sticky hand.

署.meaning: <part>Someone</part> at the bank forgets his pen, so he dips his fishing <part>net</part> in the ink pot and swipes it across the cheque, leaving a criss-cross smudge. The clerk squints, shrugs and stamps it. Nobody will ever forge that <kanji>signature</kanji>.
署.on: On the way home he buys a spare net at the bait <sound>sho</sound>p, ready for the next cheque.
